text:
emma: Heads up — p99 for text-generation jumped to ~1.9s around 10:03 UTC. Investigating shows kv/prefix cache hit-rate for several hosts fell from ~90% to ~8% in <5m. Not looking like the usual noisy tenant dump, more like mass evictions. anyone else seeing this?

mike: saw the grafana alert, coming in. Did we roll anything to kernel-selector recently?

jon: rolled kernel-selector-v2 to canary at 09:58 (10% of traffic). It changes kernel choice scoring: favors newer fused kernels for seq_len > 64. No KV/cache changes in the same rollout AFAIK.

emma: timeline matches. drop started ~09:59. metrics-bot can you paste the hitrate and eviction graphs?

metrics-bot: host-metrics: https://internal.grafana/redwood/d/kv_cache/kv-hitrate?from=1699999200000&to=1699999800000 — host cluster a3 shows eviction-rate spike concurrent with canary.

sara: quick thought — if kernel-v2 path increases per-request memory for KV shards (e.g., different KV prefetch or prefix grouping), it could reduce effective cache capacity and trigger evictions. Any memory accounting changes in the selector?

jon: kernel-v2 doesn't touch KV code intentionally. But it switches execution kernels which change live allocations during decoding (temp buffers). I didn't expect it to affect long-lived KV pages.

mike: grabbing hot profiler from one affected host. attaching tail logs:

```
2026-03-18T09:59:21Z host-a3-12: kv_cache: evict shard=27 freed=12MB cause=memory_pressure
2026-03-18T09:59:21Z host-a3-12: runtime: kernel-selector: chosen kernel=fused-mha-v2 seq_len=96
2026-03-18T09:59:21Z host-a3-12: batching: active_batches=14 avg_batch_size=6
2026-03-18T09:59:22Z host-a3-12: kv_cache: miss prefix=tenant-214/prefix-0
```

mike: looks like many requests with seq_len ~90 hit fused kernel, memory spike -> local eviction -> prefix misses -> downstream latency.

emma: tenant-214 popped up in traces a few times, but not enough QPS to explain full collapse. Could be kernel path increases transient working set across many shards.

jon: hypothesize: kernel-selector-v2 scoring overprefers fused kernels for medium-long sequences which increase ephemeral memory demand. With our per-host soft-cache-limit, the extra transient usage pushes us over threshold and we bleed cached entries.

sara: can we sanity-check by forcing kernel-selector back to v1 on canary hosts? If hit-rate recovers, we know cause.

mike: I can flip the rollout to 0% for the canary group. deploy-bot, rollback canary kernel-selector-v2 id=csr-2026-03-18-09:58?

deploy-bot: rollback started for rollout csr-2026-03-18-09:58. Affected hosts: a3-*. Progress: 0/12 -> 6/12 -> 12/12.

metrics-bot: After rollback complete (10:08 UTC) host-metrics: eviction-rate down, prefix hit-rate recovering to ~88% within 3m, p99 back to ~430ms.

emma: ok rollback validates hypothesis. Root cause probably kernel-selector-v2 memory pattern. We need a patch: add transient memory guard to kernel selector and a simulated allocation test to validate cache headroom before applying fused kernel on a host.

jon: working on patch. Immediate mitigations: 1) revert canary (done), 2) add guard that requires free_cache_mb > X before selecting fused-mha-v2, 3) add smoke test that exercises decoding mem use on preprod.

mike: also fine to add a metric exposing selector-chosen-kernel vs host_free_cache to alert earlier.

emma: agree. action items: jon will open PR for kernel selector guard and test (owner: jon). mike will add alert/metric for kernel_choice vs cache_headroom (owner: mike). sara will triple-check soft-cache-limit behavior and whether tenants can be unfairly evicted (owner: sara). I'll write a short postmortem note and notify customer-ops for any affected tenants.

jon: PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pull/7421 "kernel selector: require cache headroom for fused kernels" — includes unit + smoke test.

mike: added grafana panel and alert rule: "kernel-selected-with-low-cache-headroom" — firing threshold low for now.

emma: pairing note — suspicious variant: some hosts were running older kernel runtime that had a small memory accounting bug; combined effect amplified eviction. sara can you list hosts with mixed runtime versions?

sara: found 3 hosts with older runtime (a3-7, a3-9, a3-11). I kicked rolling upgrade to align runtimes; they were out-of-date due to a stuck upgrade job. Will correlate after all upgrades.

mike: follow-up: looking at traces — when eviction spike happens, small requests that previously hit prefix cache now do full KV fetch adding ~40-80ms per request and causing CPU pressure too. Compound effect explains p99.

emma: lesson: kernel selector changes are non-local — they can alter transient memory profile and interact with cache heuristics. We should add a canary checklist item: simulate KV-heavy traffic with realistic prefix locality to measure cache pressure before enabling new kernel heuristics.

jon: agreed. will add to rollout playbook.

emma: thanks all. marking as resolved for now — will watch the alert for 24h. :white_check_mark:

mike: on-call handoff to sara in 2h, I'll leave traces + profiler artifacts in the incident folder.

sara: acknowledged. will monitor and follow-up if anything recurs. :eyes:
